# Bintje (01, engineer) — SPD-040

## Brief
Objective: the Bash hook must treat a read-write redirection as a write. Today IN_REDIRECTS in bin/spud_ledger.py holds "<>", so separate_redirects drops its operand unchecked and analyse_command records no redirect; `echo x 1<>ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md` overwrites the start of a protected file (Laws 1 and 5) with nothing refused. `<>` opens O_RDWR|O_CREAT in bash 3.2 and zsh 5.9, so every form writes or creates its target: bare `<>file`, `n<>file` with any fd digit prefix, spaced and unspaced operands, and the same inside `sh -c`/`bash -c`/`zsh -c`, `eval` and subshell strings. Move `<>` to the output side so its operand is kept as a target and goes through every check an output target gets today: path rule, glob and brace readings of the target (SPD-034, SPD-039, SPD-041), directory changes before it (redirect_cwds), and Spud's own ledger and state-directory rules.

Work red first (superpowers TDD): probe both shells in the scratchpad with a throwaway file to confirm each form writes or creates, add a test class to tests/test_hooks.py whose cases fail on the unchanged code, then fix. Check every other place IN_REDIRECTS or the redirect operator sets are read (for example the `op in OUT_REDIRECTS or op in IN_REDIRECTS` branch near analyse_segment) so `<>` is not read as input anywhere else. Keep plain input redirections (`<`, `<<`, `<<<`, `<&`) unchanged, and add controls that they still pass. If you find a related write form the hook misses that is outside this brief (for example a named-fd `{fd}<>file` or `{fd}>file` in zsh), probe it and file a proposal rather than fixing it.

Done when: the new test class is red on the unchanged code and green after; the full suite passes (`python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, run it in the background, about three and a half minutes; report the new count); a before/after differential over the existing test command strings loses no finding and changes only `<>` lines; hook latency stays within a millisecond of today's.

Deliverables: bin/spud_ledger.py and tests/test_hooks.py only. Read first: ledger/tickets/SPD-040.md; separate_redirects, IN_REDIRECTS and OUT_REDIRECTS in bin/spud_ledger.py; the Result sections of ledger/teams/SPUD-041/Roseval.md and SPUD-039's members for how redirect targets and glob readings are checked today.

## Ticket proposals
- **Bash hook: >, >>, >|, &> and &>> into a file named by digits or - are skipped as a descriptor** — suggested P3; created as [[SPD-045]] at P3 by Spud.
  Why: separate_redirects drops any operand that is all digits or - for every output operator, but only >& reads such a word as a descriptor or a close. The other operators write a file of that name, so a member writes outside its deliverables (cd docs && echo x > 3) and Spud writes a file past Law 1, with nothing checked. No generated ledger file has such a name, so the harm is bounded to a stray file in a protected directory.
  Evidence: Probe (SPD-040, scratchpad, zsh 5.9 -f -o nobareglobqual and bash 3.2): echo x > 3, >> 3, >| 3 and &> 3 created a file named 3 in both shells, &>> 3 in zsh (a syntax error in bash 3.2); > -, >> - and &> - created a file named -; 2> 12 created 12. Only >& 3 and >& - were a descriptor and a close. analyse_command('echo x >3') and ('echo x >-') record redirects []. Fix sketch: skip a digit or - operand only after >& (and keep &-prefixed operands skipped).

## Result
Produced (worktree spd-040-read-write-redirect, uncommitted): bin/spud_ledger.py and tests/test_hooks.py only.

THE FIX. The read-write redirection <> is now an output redirection. It moved from IN_REDIRECTS to OUT_REDIRECTS, and separate_redirects keeps its operand as a target whatever the operand's shape. Before, the hook dropped the operand unchecked, so echo x 1<>ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md overwrote a generated file with nothing refused. Every <> target now gets every check an output target gets: the path rule, the glob, brace and zsh-pattern readings (SPD-034/039/041), redirect_cwds after a cd or a compound command, the state directory, Law 1, and the rule that a Spud call's allow needs every redirect quiet. The other readers of the sets were checked. mark_zsh_patterns tests OUT|IN together and the heredoc test names << and <<- only, so neither changes. Input redirections <, <<, <<-, <<<, <& are unchanged.

PROBES (scratchpad files only; zsh 5.9 -f, zsh -f -o nobareglobqual, bash 3.2, sh): every <> form created or wrote its file. That covers bare <>f, spaced <> f, the fd prefixes 0, 1, 2, 9 and 10, the leading form <>f echo x, a quoted operand, <>f<>g (both files), and the same inside sh -c, bash -c, zsh -c, eval, a subshell and $(). printf abcd > g; echo x 1<>g left x then cd. <>3 and <>- created files named 3 and -. 1<>&2 is a syntax error in both shells, so <> has no dup form, hence the operand is always a file name. exec {fd}<>f created f in every shell. echo x {fd}>f was already recorded as a redirect, so the named-fd forms need nothing more.

TESTS. ReadWriteRedirectTest has 9 methods: the evidence (both members and Spud, plus the analysis records the target), every spelling, operand shapes (3, -, deliverables), shell strings, eval, subshells, substitutions, compounds, pipes and env sh -c, glob, brace, (a|b) and <n-m> operands and no-match, directories (cd, compound redirect_cwds, cd $DIR, ~+), the state directory (1<>.spud/pycache/x escapes DB_PATH_RE, so the target check is what refuses it) and a variable target, a spud call with <> no longer allowed (<>/dev/null still is), and controls for input redirections. Red: run from a scratchpad copy of the unchanged bin with the final tests, 8 of 9 methods fail (121 failures) and the controls pass. Green on the fix. Full suite from the worktree: Ran 522 tests, OK (513 before). CLAUDE.md suite count becomes 522.

DIFFERENTIAL. Old against new analyse_command over 2241 string literals in tests/test_hooks.py (2119 existed before this change): 92 read differently.
